target.title: fix(codex): honor timeoutSeconds for dynamic tool calls when timeoutMs is absent
target.body:
Fixes #98864.

## What Problem This Solves

Codex dynamic tool calls can specify `timeoutSeconds` while omitting `timeoutMs`. `resolveDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs` currently only reads `timeoutMs`, so a tool configured with a seconds-only timeout falls back to the default 90s deadline instead of honoring the caller's intent.

## Why This Change Was Made

`readDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs` now falls back to `readTimeoutSecondsAsMs(value.timeoutSeconds)` when `timeoutMs` is absent or invalid. The existing `readTimeoutSecondsAsMs` helper (already used for configured image timeouts) converts a positive finite seconds value to milliseconds. `timeoutMs` still takes precedence when both are present.

## User Impact

Dynamic tools that pass `timeoutSeconds` (e.g. session send helpers) now get the expected per-call hard timeout instead of silently using the default.

## Evidence

Regression test:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts
```

```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  16 passed (16)
```

Real behavior proof:

```bash
node_modules/.bin/tsx scripts/proof/codex-dynamic-tool-timeout-seconds.mts
```

The proof calls the real `resolveDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs` with the three cases from the issue:

```
=== Proof: Codex dynamic tool timeoutSeconds support ===

timeoutSeconds only: expected 30000ms, got 30000ms PASS
timeoutMs takes precedence: expected 5000ms, got 5000ms PASS
non-positive timeoutSeconds falls back to default: expected 90000ms, got 90000ms PASS

All cases passed.
```
